'''Ursula''' is the colloquial name for the '''Central Processing Center''', the largest [[U.S. Customs and Border Protection]] detention center for undocumented immigrants. The facility is a retrofitted warehouse that can hold more than 1,000 people.<ref>{{Cite conference|last=Department of Homeland Security. Office of Inspector General|date=2018-09-28|title=Results of Unannounced Inspections of Conditions for Unaccompanied Alien Children in CBP Custody|url=https://www.oig.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/assets/2018-10/OIG-18-87-Sep18.pdf|page=4}}</ref> It was opened in 2014 on W. Ursula Avenue in [[McAllen, Texas]]. In June 2018, it gained notoriety for the practice of keeping children in large [[cage]]s made of [[chain-link fencing]].<ref name="Ryan 2018"/><ref name=Frej/>

== About ==
The center, better known as "Ursula," is the largest immigration processing and detention center run by the [[United States Border Patrol|Border Patrol]] and the [[U.S. Customs and Border Protection|Customs and Border Protection Agency]].<ref name="Ryan 2018" />
The detention and processing center was opened in 2014 at 3700 W. Ursula Avenue in McAllen, Texas.<ref name="Findell 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.themonitor.com/news/local/article_b22a23ae-0e2b-11e4-b9d3-0017a43b2370.html|title=Border Patrol opens central processing facility for unaccompanied kids|last=Findell|first=Elizabeth|date=17 July 2014|work=The Monitor|access-date=18 June 2018}}</ref> The facility is made from a former [[warehouse]] which was leased by the federal government and modified to be able to hold 1,000 children.<ref name="Findell 2018" /> Children were kept in cages made of [[chain-link fencing]] inside of the 77,000 square-foot warehouse.<ref name="Findell 2018" /><ref name="Ryan 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thecut.com/2018/06/inside-ursula-border-patrol-center-family-separation.html|title=Inside 3 Detention Centers Where Immigrant Children Are Kept From Their Parents|last=Ryan|first=Lisa|date=18 June 2018|work=The Cut|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618222337/https://www.thecut.com/2018/06/inside-ursula-border-patrol-center-family-separation.html|archive-date=18 June 2018|language=en}}</ref>

Minors who arrive at the [[Mexico–United States border]] unaccompanied or who have been separated from their families are supposed to only stay in this type of processing center for under 72 hours.<ref name="Ryan 2018" /> After processing, minors are sent to facilities run by the [[United States Department of Health and Human Services|Department of Health and Human Services]].<ref name=Frej>{{Cite news|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/images-inside-center-immigrants_us_5b27bebae4b0f9178a9f6f7f|title=These Are The Texas Immigration Center Photos Stirring Anti-Trump Outrage|last=Frej|first=Willa|date=2018-06-18|work=Huffington Post|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618224954/https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/images-inside-center-immigrants_us_5b27bebae4b0f9178a9f6f7f|archive-date=18 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> The facility also houses adults and individuals are separated based on how they crossed into the United States.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mcallen-texas-immigration-facility-separated-families-today-2018-06-18/|title=Inside the Texas facility housing hundreds of illegal immigrants|last=Begnaud|first=David|date=18 June 2018|work=CBS News|access-date=2018-06-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619001212/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mcallen-texas-immigration-facility-separated-families-today-2018-06-18/|archive-date=19 June 2018|language=en}}</ref>

Filming or photography is not allowed inside of the facility.<ref name="Ryan 2018" /> During the weekend of June 16, 2018, reporters were allowed to tour the facility (without cameras).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/national-international/Children-Border-Patrol-Facility-South-Texas-485804601.html|title=Kids in Cages With Mylar Blankets in Texas Border Facility|last=Ciechalski|first=Suzanne|date=18 June 2018|work=NBC Chicago|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618225301/https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/national-international/Children-Border-Patrol-Facility-South-Texas-485804601.html|archive-date=18 June 2018|language=en}}</ref>

[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] reported in June 2019 that Dolly Lucio Sevier, a board-certified doctor, visited Ursula after a flu outbreak at the facility that resulted in five infants requiring to enter a [[neonatal intensive care unit]]. Sevier wrote that a medical declaration that the "conditions within which [the migrant minors] are held could be compared to torture facilities ... extreme cold temperatures, lights on 24 hours a day, no adequate access to medical care, basic sanitation, water, or adequate food." All of the 39 children she assessed showed signs of [[Psychological trauma|trauma]].<ref name="ABCsevier">{{cite web |last1=Marshall |first1=Serena |last2=Zak |first2=Lana |last3=Metz |first3=Jennifer |title=Doctor compares conditions for unaccompanied children at immigrant holding centers to 'torture facilities' |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/doctor-compares-conditions-immigrant-holding-centers-torture-facilities/story?id=63879031 |website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref>
